```markdown
[Date]

Harper Hayes
[Member street address]
[City, State ZIP]

Tufts Health Plan
Appeals Department
[Appeal address exactly as printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination — Rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827)**
- **Member:** Harper Hayes
- **Member ID:** W668248955
- **Reference number:** POC-E8E7B452F1-10979
- **Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-15
- **Governing policy:** Evolent Shoulder Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet (Evolent_CG-318) — https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2024-02/2023%20Shldr%20Arthroscopy%20Clin%20Tip%20Sheet%20Evolent%2002282024.pdf

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for the rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827) requested by my surgeon, Marchetti, MD. The notice dated 2026-08-15 states that the clinical records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the plan's own published criteria and the records in my file point the other way.

I am citing only the Evolent Shoulder Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet (Evolent_CG-318), linked above.

---

## 1. My MRI places my tear in the category for which the plan's policy does not require non-operative treatment

The plan's policy states:

> "Medium or large tear full-thickness tear (1-5 cm) – non-operative treatment not required."

My MRI of the shoulder dated 2026-07-09 shows a **full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm**, with grade 2 fatty atrophy. A 1.8 cm full-thickness tear falls within the 1–5 cm range quoted above. By the plan's own written criteria, a trial of non-operative treatment is not a requirement for a tear of this size and type — yet non-operative treatment is the sole reason given for the denial.

The policy also explains why tear size is the deciding factor:

> "Because the management of rotator cuff pathology is dependent on the size of the tear, an MRI is required for ALL requests and the actual report radiology should be submitted."

and

> "As best possible, the size of the tear should be stated in the office notes and documentation should be provided if the requesting physician disagrees with the MRI reading."

The MRI was performed and reported, and the measured size is in the record. If the plan's reviewer applied the conservative-care requirements that the policy attaches to a different tear category, I ask that the determination be corrected. If the reviewer instead concluded that my tear belongs in a different category, I ask the plan to tell me which category it used and what measurement it relied on.

## 2. The records contain each item the policy says office notes should document

The policy states:

> "Office notes for all shoulder arthroscopy requests should document: o Symptom onset, duration, and severity; o Loss of function and/or limitations; o Type and duration of non-operative management modalities (where applicable). o Radiographic findings (MRI reports must be provided)"

Matching my records to that list:

| What the policy asks for | What my records show |
| --- | --- |
| Symptom onset, duration, and severity | 12 months of progressive shoulder pain, unrelieved by rest; positive provocative testing on the affected side; range of motion limited by pain |
| Loss of function and/or limitations | I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height, and I cannot sleep on the affected side |
| Type and duration of non-operative management | Supervised physical therapy for rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, 8 weeks (2026-05-08 to 2026-07-03), 24 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note; NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief; corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-13 with 4 weeks of partial relief |
| Radiographic findings, MRI report provided | MRI of the shoulder, 2026-07-09: full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy |

## 3. Even measured against the policy's conservative-care language, my treatment is documented

Although the quoted policy language does not require non-operative treatment for a full-thickness tear in the 1–5 cm range, my records document a substantial course of it. The policy's list of non-operative options includes:

> "Physical therapy or properly instructed home exercise program;"

> "Minimum of 4 weeks of oral NSAIDs (if not medically contraindicated);"

> "Single injection of corticosteroid and local anesthetic into subacromial or intra- articular space"

I completed 24 supervised physical therapy visits over 8 weeks, took NSAIDs for 6 months — well beyond the four-week minimum the policy names — and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-13 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief. The policy also states:

> "A cortisone injection is not required for ANY rotator cuff repair requests. It is only one of several non-operative treatment options."

I had the injection in any event, and it did not resolve my symptoms.

I want to be precise about one point: several provisions of this policy end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that are not reproduced in the excerpts available to me — for example, the introductory lines for partial tears, for small full-thickness tears under 1 cm, and for massive tears over 5 cm. I am not attempting to characterize criteria I have not seen, and the denial notice did not identify which criteria were applied to my request. **I ask the plan to state in writing the specific criterion or criteria from this policy that my records were found not to meet.**

---

## What I am asking for

I respectfully ask the plan to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-15 (reference POC-E8E7B452F1-10979) and authorize the rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827, as requested by my surgeon, Marchetti, MD, whose submitted records document my symptoms, my loss of function, my course of non-operative care, and the MRI findings. If the denial is upheld in whole or in part, please send me the specific policy criteria relied upon, the clinical rationale, and the credentials of the reviewer who made the decision, along with instructions for the next level of review.

I understand that my appeal must be received by **2027-02-11**, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice. I am submitting this appeal **in writing** to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand the plan also accepts appeals **verbally by phone at 888-257-1985** or **in person**, and that if the plan issues a final internal denial, I may request **external review within 4 months of that final internal decision**.

Enclosed for the reviewer's file:
- Denial notice dated 2026-08-15
- MRI report of the shoulder, 2026-07-09
- Physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-05-08 to 2026-07-03
- Office notes from Marchetti, MD
- [Any additional records I wish to include]

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this request.

Sincerely,

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
Harper Hayes
Member ID: W668248955
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date signed]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
```

evidence.policy_title: Evolent Shoulder Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet (Evolent_CG-318)
quotes: Office notes for all shoulder arthroscopy requests should document: o Symptom onset, duration, and severity; o Loss of function and/or limitations; o Type and duration of non-operative management modalities (where applicable). o Radiographic findings (MRI reports must be provided)
Because the management of rotator cuff pathology is dependent on the size of the tear, an MRI is required for ALL requests and the actual report radiology should be submitted.
A cortisone injection is not required for ANY rotator cuff repair requests. It is only one of several non-operative treatment options.
Partial tear: Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least three of the following criteria:
Minimum of 4 weeks of oral NSAIDs (if not medically contraindicated);

Small full-thickness tear (< 1cm): Failure of at least 6 weeks of non-operative treatment, including physical therapy or a properly instructed home exercise program (that includes exercises for scapular dyskinesis when present) AND at least one of the following:
Medium or large tear full-thickness tear (1-5 cm) – non-operative treatment not required.

Massive (> 5 cm and at least 2tendons involved), Full-Thickness Rotator Cuff Tear Surgical repair of a massive torn rotator cuff including partial repair and Superior Capsular Reconstruction may be necessary when ALL of the following criteria are met:
MRI demonstrates no advanced fatty changes (Goutallier stage 0 (normal muscle), 1 (some fatty streaks), or 2 (less than 50% fatty degeneration or infiltration)
Physical therapy or properly instructed home exercise program;
Single injection of corticosteroid and local anesthetic into subacromial or intra- articular space
As best possible, the size of the tear should be stated in the office notes and documentation should be provided if the requesting physician disagrees with the MRI reading.
No x-ray evidence of chronic subacromial articulation of humeral head, distance between acromion and humeral head
MRI or Ultrasound showing massive (> 5cm), full-thickness tear (with intact or reparable subscapularis for superior capsular reconstruction)
No advanced or severe arthritis (severe narrowing of glenohumeral space or bone- on-bone articulation, large osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, or cysts, etc.)
